summary: Order submit failures (30% error rate, 504s) started at 2026-03-17T11:01:25Z and persist unchanged through the latest data (12:59Z), i.e. ~1h42m AFTER the order-service v2.15.2 rollback at 11:16Z. The 504s are order-service calls to exchange-gateway (placeOrder), which in turn is timing out against its external upstream api.exchange-partner.example (connect timeouts at 5000ms; upstream latency p99 ~9.4s vs ~120ms baseline). exchange-gateway's own resources are healthy (CPU flat ~30%, request rate flat ~270 req/s), and pricing-engine (and its 09:20 cache-TTL config change) is entirely unaffected. The evidence points to the external exchange partner API degrading — a dependency_failure — not the order-service release. The reported rollback is a red herring. Outcome: root cause identified (dependency_failure at the external exchange provider), with the caveat that the vendor has no telemetry, so the partner-side fault can only be inferred from the gateway's upstream metrics and error messages.

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner API degraded (dependency_failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The third-party exchange provider at api.exchange-partner.example began failing/hanging around 11:01Z, causing 5s connect timeouts and 503s at exchange-gateway, which returned 504s to order-service (placeOrder and quoteSnapshot both affected). order-service's release is unrelated.

causal_chain.claim: connect timeouts (5000ms) and 503s raise exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate to ~45% and upstream latency to ~9.3s
exchange-gateway returns 504 to order-service placeOrder calls

assumptions: api.exchange-partner.example has no telemetry, so the partner-side fault is inferred from gateway upstream metrics, not directly observed
quoteSnapshot timeouts (via pricing-engine path) are the same partner degradation, not a separate cause

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 release caused the failures (bad_deployment)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The order-service v2.15.2 idempotency-key release introduced a fault causing order submit failures, which is why on-call is rolling it back.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Rollback at 11:16Z did NOT restore service: 310 identical 504 errors continue through 12:58:54Z (F4). The failing call is to exchange-gateway, whose upstream to the external partner is timing out (F5-F7); order-service's own error rate onset (11:02, F2) is driven entirely by that external timeout pattern, not by submit-handler code.

ranked_hypotheses.title: exchange-gateway or its infrastructure exhausted resources (resource/capacity/infrastructure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: exchange-gateway pods ran out of CPU/memory/connections or its node failed, causing the timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: exchange-gateway cpu_pct (~30%) and request_rate (~270 req/s) are flat across onset (F8), and its latency increase is entirely in upstream_latency_ms to the external host (F7), indicating the failure is external to the gateway box.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds config change caused the incident (config_change)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 09:20Z pricing-engine cache TTL reduction from 5s to 4s increased downstream load and caused timeouts.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine latency is flat (~60ms) and it has zero errors (F9); the change is 1h41m before onset (F10); the failing host is the external exchange partner, not pricing-engine or redis-cache.

facts.statement: order-service 504 errors began 11:02:45Z and continued to 12:58:54Z, all of the form 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'.
order-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~30.8% at 11:02 and stayed ~30% through 12:59.
The only deployment was order-service v2.15.2 at 10:48Z, rolled back at 11:16Z.
exchange-gateway logged upstream connect timeouts at 5000ms to host=api.exchange-partner.example, plus 503s and a circuit-breaker OPEN warning.
exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate rose to ~45% and upstream_latency_ms to ~9.3s at onset.
exchange-gateway's own cpu_pct (~30%) and request_rate (~270 req/s) are flat across the onset.
pricing-engine is unaffected (flat ~60ms latency, zero errors) and the only config change was its 09:20Z cache TTL 5->4.
exchange-api is an external vendor node with no telemetry, reachable only via exchange-gateway.
No exchange-partner timeout errors appear before 11:01:25Z.
Historical incident HIST-103 matches the current symptom profile with root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side'.

assumptions: The 5000ms connect timeouts to api.exchange-partner.example reflect genuine partner-side slowness/unavailability rather than a local network/DNS fault on the gateway's egress path.
quoteSnapshot and placeOrder failures share the same partner root cause rather than two independent faults.
order-service v2.15.2 did not itself introduce the external timeout behavior (its placeOrder path always calls exchange-gateway).

timeline.event: pricing-engine config change cfg-2290: cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (unrelated; pricing-engine unaffected)
exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate/latency begin rising (3.7%, 817ms avg) within this bucket
First exchange-gateway 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder'
order-service error_rate jumps to ~30.8%; exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate ~45%, upstream_latency ~9.2s
Circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)
order-service errors continue unchanged after rollback (310 more through 12:58:54Z)
Latest data: order-service error_rate 30.4%, exchange-gateway upstream_latency ~9.4s — still failing

recommended_actions.action: Stop/complete the order-service rollback as a fix — it is not the cause; keep v2.15.2 (or revert only if independent reasons) and redirect effort to the exchange integration.
recommended_actions.rationale: Errors persisted 1h42m past rollback (F4); rolling back further wastes time and risks unnecessary churn.

recommended_actions.action: Engage the exchange partner / vendor support with the x-partner-request-id values (e.g. 46ed2490) and the 5000ms connect-timeout / 503 evidence; check partner status page.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failing host api.exchange-partner.example returned 503s and hung; partner-side confirmation is the fastest path.

recommended_actions.action: Fail over to a secondary exchange route / enable degraded mode (e.g. queue placeOrder retries) as was done in HIST-103.
recommended_actions.rationale: Historically resolved the same symptom profile by failing over to a secondary exchange route.

recommended_actions.action: Tune exchange-gateway resilience: shorten connect timeout/tighten circuit-breaker thresholds so partner slowness sheds load faster instead of holding 5s+ connections.
recommended_actions.rationale: 5000ms connect timeouts dominate and a 60s-window breaker opened only after ~2 min of degradation.

recommended_actions.action: Add telemetry/synthetic monitoring for the external exchange API so partner-side degradation is observable directly (it currently has has_telemetry:false).
recommended_actions.rationale: Partner has no telemetry, forcing inference from gateway metrics only.

data_gaps: api.exchange-partner.example has has_telemetry:false — the partner-side root cause cannot be directly observed; it is inferred from exchange-gateway upstream metrics and error messages only.
No vendor status/incident data was available to independently confirm the partner outage.

Logs for exchange-gateway and order-service are truncated (truncated:true, 40 of 349/473 returned); absence of other error patterns is not proven, though the top-pattern counts and metrics corroborate the single failure mode.

findings.statement: order-service errored continuously from 11:02:45Z to 12:58:54Z; all 349 ERROR entries are the same pattern: exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder).

refs.quote: exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder) orderId=07fcb25a

findings.statement: order-service error_rate sits at ~0.2% until 10:49, then jumps to ~30.8% at 11:02 and stays ~30-31% through 12:59.
The only deployment in the window is order-service v2.15.2 (Add idempotency keys to order submit), deployed 10:48:00Z and rolled back at 11:16:00Z.
order-service errors continue after the 11:16 rollback: 310 ERROR entries between 11:16:05Z and 12:58:54Z, all '504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'. The rollback did not restore service.

exchange-gateway emits errors against its external upstream: 163 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' from 11:01:25Z and 146 'quoteSnapshot' timeouts from 11:01:43Z, plus 161 'exchange-api returned 503' entries and a circuit-breaker OPEN warning.

refs.quote: upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder
circuit breaker OPEN for exchange-api (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s)

findings.statement: exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate jumps from ~0.3% (flat 08:00-10:36) to 45.46% at 11:02 and stays ~44-47% through 12:59.
exchange-gateway upstream_latency_ms rises from ~120ms baseline to ~9151ms at 11:02 (max ~10,042ms) and stays ~9.2-9.4s through 12:59.
exchange-gateway's own resource usage is flat and healthy: cpu_pct ~30% and request_rate ~270 req/s are unchanged before and after onset.
pricing-engine is unaffected: latency_p99_ms stays flat at ~59-62ms across the whole window and it has zero WARN/ERROR logs.
The only config change is pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20:00Z (config-bot), which touches pricing-engine and is 1h41m before onset.
The dependency graph confirms exchange-gateway -> exchange-api is an 'external' node owned by 'vendor' with has_telemetry:false, and order-service -> exchange-gateway is http.
No exchange-partner timeouts were logged before 11:01:25Z; a targeted query for 'timeout' on exchange-gateway from 09:00-11:05 returns only 10 entries, earliest at 11:01:25Z.

A prior incident HIST-103 (2025-10-21) has the same symptom profile — '504 on order submit', 'upstream timeouts', services order-service/exchange-gateway — with root cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side'.

findings.statement: The fault propagates outward-in: order-service 504s are a downstream symptom of exchange-gateway's upstream timeouts, whose target host is the external provider (api.exchange-partner.example).
